'''Ignace-Louis-Alfred Le Cointe''' (14 September 1823 – 18 June 1893, sometimes called '''Alfred Lecointe''') was a French mathematician, mathematics teacher, and [[Jesuit]] priest. He wrote textbooks about [[trigonometry]] and [[conic sections]] and a book of problems at the [[Secondary education|secondary]] level.

== Life ==

Le Cointe was born 14 September 1823, in [[Nîmes]], to a devout and illustrious family.<ref>{{harvnb|Boussac|1894}} mentions among his relatives several naval officers including a [[counter admiral]]; and many nobles including [[count]]s, [[viscount]]s, and [[marquis]]; a university inspector, and a [[Carmelite]] nun. Boussac says that, in his humility, Le Cointe rarely mentioned them.</ref>  He had an early interest and aptitude for exact sciences, so was sent to [[Paris]] to attend the [[École Centrale Paris|École Centrale]] at an unusually young age. In 1847, joined the Jesuit order, and was sent to study philosophy at the seminary in [[Vals-près-le-Puy|Vals]]. He taught mathematics in Vals, at the Collége Saint-Michel in [[Saint-Étienne]], at the École Sainte-Marie in [[Toulouse]], and at the [[Institut Catholique de Toulouse]]. He died in Toulouse.<ref>{{cite book |year=1900 |last=Sommervogel |first=Carlos |author-link=Carlos Sommervogel |title=Bibliothèque de la Compagnie de Jésus |edition=Nouvelle |language=fr |volume=9: Supplément: Casalicchio–Zweisig, Anonymes-Pseudonymes |place=Paris |publisher=Alphonse Picard |chapter=Lecointe, Alfred |pages=581–582 |chapter-url=https://archive.org/details/bibliothquedelac09back/page/n298/mode/1up}} <!-- An apparent derivative of this is in the Enciclopedia universal ilustrada europeo-americana, p. 1278 https://archive.org/details/enciclopediauniv0000unse_a0r1/page/1278/ --></ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Boussac |first=Louis |journal=Lettres d'Uclès |series=2e série |volume=2 |year=1894 |pages=545–549 |title=Le P. Alfred Lecointe |url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k91276085/f549.item |language=fr}} </ref>
